turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did you get a chance to look at that paper on SMART-LLM I sent over?
I did. It's quite interesting. I noted that it was published in 2024 by Kannan, Venkatesh, and Min.
Right, the authors are important for the citation. I'm worried about the formatting for the bibliography.
I can help with that. Just let me know which citation style you need.
APA 7th. Also, my coffee maker is acting up again. The light blinks but it won't start.
That sounds like a heating element issue or a water sensor blockage. Have you tried descaling it?
I'll try that tonight. For now, just make sure the citation is ready for my draft.
Understood. I have the details saved.
Lloyd, I'm back to reviewing SMART-LLM. I need to explain how it works in my presentation.
Sure. From what you shared, it encodes robot skills as Python scripts and uses programmatic prompts to map tasks to subtasks and agent assignments.
Exactly. That modular approach is the key takeaway. I'm also trying to fix the squeaky wheel on my office chair.
WD-40 usually helps with that. Or perhaps tightening the axle nut.
I have some lubricant around here somewhere. Anyway, keep that description of the methodology in mind for the slides.
I will. It's a distinctive mechanism compared to other LLM-based robot frameworks.
Agreed. It feels more transparent because of the Python aspect.
Indeed. The script-based encoding allows for easier debugging and verification.
